title: ForgeSight Feature Brief: Day One Clarity
raw_text:
ForgeSight — Feature Brief: "Day One Clarity"
Author: Marcus (Head of Product), with input from Dana (Customer Success) and Tom (Sales)
Circulated 25 August 2026

The promise

Enterprise operations teams are drowning in data they own and cannot see. ForgeSight exists to close the gap between the warehouse and the decision, and "Day One Clarity" is the release theme that makes that promise legible from the first login rather than the fortieth.

What we are building

Every ForgeSight customer lands, on sign-in, on a single Operations Overview view that summarises their four headline metrics — volume, cost, on-time rate and exceptions — without any configuration. No empty grid. No blank canvas. The first thing a customer sees is their own business.

Clarity is nothing without depth behind it. From any summary metric on the Overview, a user can drill down to the underlying transaction rows in a single click. The number and the rows behind the number are never more than one gesture apart, because a number a manager cannot interrogate is a number a manager will not trust.

Context turns a number into a judgement. Every metric in ForgeSight can be compared against the same period in the previous year, so "eleven thousand shipments" becomes "eleven thousand shipments, up nine per cent on last August". Our customers do not run their businesses in isolated weeks and neither should their dashboards.

Trust is a feature. Each chart states the warehouse table it draws from, in plain sight, on the chart. When a director and an analyst disagree about a figure, the conversation should end in four seconds, not in a fortnight of email.

And clarity should not stop at our own front door. ForgeSight will offer an embed code that places a single chart inside the customer's own intranet page, so the operations dashboard reaches the people who never log in to a dashboard.

What "day one" commits us to

The name is a promise about time, so we are making it a measurable one: a new customer's first live dashboard is standing within five business days of contract signature. Dana's team owns that clock.

Scope discipline

For the pilot, ForgeSight ships in English only. Halcyon has asked about French and the answer, for now, is a warm no.
